hyps.why: A skip on 0->3 stabilizes gradient flow so the deeper conv path on edge 5 adds usable capacity rather than redundancy.
A pooled feeder into node 2 supplies blurred features, so the conv on 2->3 gains less than with a conv feeder.
With edge 1 removed node 2 has little input, so a conv on 2->3 has less signal to transform.
Stacking two 3x3 convs along 0->1->2 gives redundant receptive field and extra optimization difficulty.
Pooling then a 1x1 conv is complementary: spatial aggregation followed by channel mixing.
Replacing the identity shortcut sacrifices its optimization benefit, so the swap gains less than filling an empty edge.
Replacing a weak parameter-free pool with a conv gives a larger upgrade than replacing a more useful operator.
A parallel 3x3 conv already on the direct 0->3 path makes another conv into node 3 redundant.
Swapping out a skip on the final edge removes an identity route, reducing the net gain of the conv.
Two parallel 1x1 convs into node 3 duplicate the same channel-mixing function.
